title: Retention Discount When No Competitive Threat Is Documented
scenario_text:
You are a Customer Success escalation lead at Rhine Analytics. Enterprise customer 'Cypress Retail' ($520K ARR) is up for renewal and is pushing for a steep discount after a rocky year.

Active policy: Renewal Retention Framework RRF-2, effective 2024-04-01. A standard renewal discount of up to 8% may be approved by the Customer Success Manager (CSM). A retention exception of up to 20% requires VP of Customer Success approval and is unlocked ONLY when the account carries a documented, active competitive-displacement risk — defined as a logged competitor evaluation in CRM or a written churn threat tied to the renewal. Anything above 20% requires the CRO.

Precedent (CS log): 2024-10-02, customer 'Bramble Media' ($480K ARR), granted an 18% retention discount approved by the VP of Customer Success. Note: 'Active bake-off vs. competitor Halcyon logged in CRM; CIO emailed a written churn threat. Retention tier justified.'

Variant facts: The Cypress account team has not logged any competitor evaluation in CRM, and there is no written churn threat on file. Cypress's stated reason is simply that it wants a lower price for the coming year after a rocky one. The CSM is proposing to match Bramble's 18%. The renewal closes in ten days and the account carries no other exception flag.
question: What is the maximum discount Rhine can offer Cypress, and through which approval path?
changed_fact: In the base, Cypress carries a documented active competitive-displacement risk (a logged Halcyon evaluation plus a written churn threat). In the variant, no competitor evaluation is logged and there is no churn threat, so the retention-tier trigger is absent.
